requirements.text: The data warehouse must support reporting and analysis on shared party information so that sales, HR, purchasing and marketing areas can be joined back to a single, consistent view of a person or organisation.
The business must maintain a register of business entities, the umbrella concept covering all customers, vendors and employees.
Each business entity must be identified by a single company-wide business entity number that is unique across every party, regardless of whether the party is a customer, a vendor or an employee.

The business entity number must be usable to link a party to information held in other business areas such as sales, purchasing and HR, making the party register the integration point for the company.
requirements.action: link party to other areas using business entity number

requirements.text: The business must be able to recognise that the same party may play more than one role at the same time, for example an employee who is also a retail customer.
requirements.obj: multiple concurrent roles of a party

requirements.text: A party must not be forced into a single role.
Each business entity record must carry a last-changed timestamp recording when it was last updated, so the business can understand the currency of the party register.
Each business entity must carry a globally unique record identifier that supports data replication between systems.
The globally unique record identifier has no business meaning, is not a business key, must be treated as technical metadata and needs no business reporting.

The source area records only the existence of a business entity and its last-change timestamp, not the kind of party, its first registration date or its active status, so party lifecycle reporting cannot be derived from this area.
The business must record every person it deals with, identified by the same company-wide business entity number, without a separate person identifier.
Every person must be a business entity and use the business entity number as their identifier, although not every business entity is a person.
The business must record the primary type of each person, which classifies why the person exists in the systems.
The recognised person types are store contact, individual (retail) customer, salesperson, employee (non-sales), vendor contact and general contact.
The business must be able to count, segment and filter people by their primary type in every analysis, since person type is a key reporting dimension.
The list of person types is a small, fixed set of codes held in the person record itself rather than in a separate reference list.
The warehouse must present the meaning of each person type code in business language rather than as the two-letter code.
The business must record each person's first name, middle name or middle initial, and last name.
The business must record an optional courtesy title, such as Mr. or Ms., for use in correspondence.
The business must record an optional surname suffix, such as Sr. or Jr.
The business must record a name style indicating whether a person's name is presented in western order (first name then last name) or eastern order (last name then first name).
Any report or output that displays a person's full name must be able to honour the recorded name style and must not assume western ordering.
Middle name, title and suffix are optional, and reporting must cope with people who have none of them.
The business must record each person's email promotion preference, which expresses the consent given for marketing contact.
The recognised email promotion preference levels are: no email promotions, email promotions from AdventureWorks only, and email promotions from AdventureWorks and selected partners.

Marketing and campaign selection must be able to filter by email promotion preference and distinguish the company-only case from the company-and-partners case, because the two permit different uses of the person's details.

The business must be able to state what a person's email promotion preference was historically, not only the current value, and the warehouse must introduce historical tracking of consent changes if an audit trail is required.
Consent is a compliance-sensitive attribute.
The source records only the current email promotion preference plus a last-changed timestamp, so consent history is not provided by the source.
The business must retain additional contact information held for a person in a free-form structured XML format.
The business must retain demographic information collected from online shoppers, such as hobbies and income, which is captured for sales analysis.
Demographic content must be made analysable, for example for segmenting customers by income band or interest, rather than stored as an opaque block.
Access to demographic and additional contact information must be treated as sensitive and restricted separately from ordinary name and contact reporting.
Each person record must carry a last-changed timestamp so the business can know how current a person's details are and identify records not touched for a long time.
The business must record the email addresses of people.
A person may have more than one email address, each numbered within the person, and the business must be able to report all of a person's addresses.
An email address belongs to exactly one person and is meaningless without that person.
The business must be able to identify people who have no email address, since they cannot be reached by email campaigns regardless of their promotion preference.
Each email address must carry its own last-changed timestamp so the business can see when a person's email details were last touched independently of the rest of their record.
The warehouse must retain historical superseded email addresses so the business can tell whether an address currently on file is the one previously used in a campaign.
The source keeps only the current email address value and does not provide historical retention of superseded addresses.
The source does not mark any email address as primary or preferred when a person has several.
The business must record the telephone numbers of people.
A person may have several telephone numbers, each qualified by the kind of phone number it is.
The business must maintain a reference list of phone number types, each with a name describing the kind of number, such as home, work or mobile.
Reporting must be able to select a person's telephone number by type, for example the work number of every store contact in Bavaria.
A telephone number belongs to exactly one person.
Each recorded telephone number must carry its own last-changed timestamp.
The business needs consistent naming of phone number types over time, because renaming a type affects the meaning of historical reporting.
The business must record a sign-in credential for a person, consisting of a protected (hashed) password value and the random value used to protect it.
The sign-in credential relates to the person's email account, indicating that people can sign in to company systems such as the online store.
Credentials must never be brought into the warehouse as readable values, reported on, or exposed to analysts.

The only business-relevant facts about a credential are whether a person has one and when it was last changed, indicating whether the person has a self-service account and how recently it was maintained.
If the business does not need to know whether a person has a credential and when it was last changed, the whole credential record should be excluded from scope.
A credential is attached to its person by the business entity number and carries no description of the person.
One person has at most one credential.
The business must record postal addresses, each identified by its own address number.
An address consists of a first street address line, an optional second street address line, a city, a postal code, and the state or province in which it sits.
The state or province determines the country, so the country of an address is known indirectly through its state or province rather than being stated on the address itself.

The business must record the geographic location (latitude and longitude) of an address to support mapping, distance and territory analysis, such as showing reseller stores on a map or measuring how far customers are from a store.
Addresses must be reportable at each geographic level: street, city, postal code, state or province, and country or region.
Each address carries a last-changed timestamp so the business can see when address details were corrected.

An address is recorded once and can be shared by more than one party, such as several employees of the same reseller store or a household; the business must not assume an address belongs to a single party.

The business needs to decide whether historical address values must be retained so that past activity can be reported against the address as it stood at the time, since address records can be edited in place and later corrections may affect analysis of where a customer was at the time of a past order.
The business must record which addresses belong to which business entity, and in what capacity.
A party can have several addresses, and the same address can serve several parties.
Every party-address relationship must carry an address type stating the role the address plays for that party.
Examples of address types given by the business are Billing, Home and Shipping.
A party may have different addresses for different purposes, for example one address to bill and another to ship to.
The combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique.
A party may hold the same address under two different address types, such as an address that is both billing and shipping, and both must be visible.
The business must maintain a reference list of address types, each with a descriptive name.
The business must be able to answer what the shipping address of a given customer is.
The business must be able to answer which customers ship to a given city.
Each party-address relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.

The source holds only the currently valid set of party-address relationships; if the business needs to know which address a party used at a past point in time, the warehouse must build and keep that history.
The business must be able to identify parties with no address on file, since these cannot be shipped to or invoiced by post.
The business must maintain a reference list of countries and regions, each identified by its ISO standard country or region code and carrying its name.
The business must maintain a reference list of states and provinces, each identified by its own number and carrying an ISO standard state or province code and a descriptive name.
Every state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.
A country or region may contain many states or provinces, and some may contain none.
The system carries a flag on a state or province indicating that no genuine state or province code exists and that the country or region code is being used in its place.
Reporting must handle states or provinces flagged as having no genuine code gracefully and must not present a substituted country code as if it were a real state code.
Every state or province is assigned to a sales territory, linking where an address is to the part of the sales organisation responsible for it.
The business must be able to roll addresses, and therefore customers, stores and employees, up to sales territory via their state or province, to support territory-level sales and coverage reporting.
Only the assignment of a state or province to a sales territory is available in this area, so the warehouse must obtain territory descriptions from the sales area.

The business can change the territory assignment of a state or province, which retrospectively changes every historical geographic roll-up; the business must decide whether territory assignments should be tracked over time so that past performance can be reported on the territory structure that applied at the time.
requirements.obj: tracking of territory assignments over time

requirements.text: Country, state and territory reference lists each carry a last-changed timestamp.
Country and state or province names used in customer-facing output and reporting must be consistent and current.
requirements.obj: country and state or province names

requirements.text: Renames of countries and states or provinces must be visible rather than silent.
requirements.obj: country and state or province names

requirements.text: The business must record which people act as contacts for which organisations, such as the named individual who is the contact at a reseller store or at a supplier.
A contact relationship links two parties: the organisation (a business entity) and the person acting as its contact.
Every contact relationship must carry a contact type describing the role the person plays for that organisation.
The business must maintain a reference list of contact types, each with a descriptive name.
The same organisation may have several contacts, each in a different role.
The combination of organisation, person and role makes a contact relationship unique.
The same person may act as a contact for more than one organisation, and may hold more than one role at the same organisation.
The business must be able to answer who the contact at a given store is, and in what role.
The business must be able to answer which organisations a given person represents.
Each contact relationship carries its own last-changed timestamp.

The source holds only the current set of contact relationships; if the business needs to know who the contact was at a given time, for example when investigating a past order, the warehouse must retain that history.

Reporting must clearly distinguish which side of a contact relationship is the organisation and which is the individual, using the party's role, because both sides use the same party number and the relationship itself does not label them.
requirements.obj: organisation and individual in contact relationship

requirements.text: The business needs a single view of a party bringing together, for one party number, the party's name and type, all email addresses, all telephone numbers with types, all addresses with types, and all organisations they are a contact for.

Reporting must correctly reflect that a party's email addresses, telephone numbers, addresses and contact relationships are one-to-many relationships, and must not assume a person has exactly one address, email or phone number.
The single view of a party must remain correct when a party plays several roles at once.
Every record in this area carries only a last modified timestamp, and the operational system holds the current state only, overwriting previous values in place.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's name, so past activity can be reported against the details that applied at the time.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's marketing consent.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of a person's email addresses and telephone numbers.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of change of an address's street, city or postal details.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of which addresses a party uses and for what purpose.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of who is a contact for an organisation and in what role.
The warehouse must preserve the full history of which sales territory a state or province belongs to.
The last-changed timestamp on each record is the only change signal the source provides, and its reliability needs to be confirmed with the operational system owners.
The source provides no deletion marker or status flag in this area, so a removed party, address or relationship simply disappears.
The business must state whether removals of parties, addresses or relationships need to be detected and retained.
The business needs visibility of people without an email address.
The business needs visibility of people without a phone number.
The business needs visibility of people without any address.
The business needs visibility of duplicate people, meaning the same individual registered more than once under different party numbers, because this affects customer counts and campaign accuracy.
The business needs visibility of addresses whose geographic location is missing, since these cannot be mapped or measured for territory purposes.
Reporting should highlight states or provinces carrying the no-genuine-code flag rather than hide them, as they signal incomplete geographic reference data.
requirements.obj: states or provinces with no genuine code

requirements.text: Reference lists (address type, contact type, phone number type, country or region, state or province) must be complete so that every relationship and address resolves to a named type, country or region.
Unresolvable references to reference lists are a data quality defect and must be reported.

This area holds personal data about identifiable individuals, including names, home addresses, private email addresses, telephone numbers, geographic coordinates, marketing consent, and self-declared demographics including income.
Access to person-level detail must be restricted to roles with a legitimate business need.
Aggregated reporting, such as counts by region, by person type and by consent level, should be available more widely.
Sign-in credentials must be excluded from all analytical use.
Marketing consent must be respected by every downstream use of the data, including any extract that leaves the warehouse.
The distinction between consent for our company only and consent for our company and partners must be carried through to any sharing decision.
The business must be able to answer, for an individual, what personal data it holds about them across this area, supported by the single view of a party.
requirements.obj: personal data held about an individual

requirements.text: The company-wide party number is assumed to be stable and never re-used for a different party; this must be confirmed with the operational system owners.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-003 states each business entity is identified by a single company-wide, unique business entity number; REQ-004 and REQ-076 confirm it is the integration point and assumed stable and never re-used (to be confirmed with source owners). Satisfies unique, stable, business-recognised, non-null.
REQ-008 and REQ-009 explicitly state the globally unique record identifier is technical replication metadata, not a business key. Listed only to document its rejection.
REQ-011 and REQ-012 state every person is identified by the company-wide business entity number with no separate person identifier; it is unique, stable and non-null for persons.

REQ-036 says addresses are numbered within the person, so the number combined with the owning person's business entity number (REQ-037) identifies an email address. The number alone is only unique within a person.
The email address value is used by the business (REQ-035) but is not stated to be unique and can change (REQ-040, REQ-041), so it is a weak key.

REQ-043 to REQ-047 describe telephone numbers as belonging to exactly one person and qualified by type. A number is identified in the context of the person and phone number type, so it needs BusinessEntityID and PhoneNumberTypeID as a composite. Uniqueness by the number alone is not stated.

REQ-045 describes a reference list of phone number types with names such as home, work or mobile. No business code is given, so the identifier is the only available key. It is a system-assigned ID, so the score is moderate to low.
REQ-045 describes the name as the business description of the type, but REQ-049 warns that types can be renamed, which makes it unstable as a key.
REQ-001-2 states each postal address is identified by its own address number. It is unique and non-null. It is business-assigned in the requirements, although no natural alternative exists.

REQ-016-2 describes a reference list of address types, and REQ-011-2 requires every party-address relationship to carry one. No business code is stated, so this identifier is the practical key, although it is system-assigned.
REQ-012-2 gives business-recognised names such as Billing, Home and Shipping, but the names could be renamed over time.
REQ-014-2 states that the combination of party, address and address type makes a party-address relationship unique. REQ-015-2 confirms the same address can be held under several types.
REQ-040-2 states that the combination of organisation, person and role makes a contact relationship unique. REQ-036-2 and REQ-037-2 define the participants and the contact type.
REQ-038-2 describes a reference list of contact types with descriptive names. No business code is given, so the identifier is the practical key, although it is system-assigned.
REQ-038-2 describes the name as the business description of the type. It is not stated to be unique or stable.
REQ-022-2 states each country or region is identified by its ISO standard code. It is a standard, stable, unique, business-recognised and non-null code.
REQ-023-2 states each state or province is identified by its own number. It is unique and non-null, although it is system-assigned.

REQ-023-2 says the ISO standard code is carried on each state or province. REQ-026-2 and REQ-066 say some have no genuine code and the country code is substituted, so it is not reliably unique or populated. It would need to be combined with CountryRegionCode.

schema.name: ModifiedDate

contracts.name: BusinessEntityContact

schema.name: PersonID

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: PersonType

schema.name: Title

schema.name: FirstName
schema.description: Given name of the person.

schema.name: MiddleName

schema.name: LastName
schema.description: Family name of the person.

schema.name: EmailPromotion

schema.name: Demographics

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique row identifier (GUID) assigned in the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID

schema.name: PhoneNumber
schema.description: The phone number of the person, as recorded in the source.

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID
schema.description: Identifier of the type of phone number (e.g. cell, home, work); references the PhoneNumberType record.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: PhoneNumberType

schema.name: PhoneNumberTypeID

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

schema.name: StateProvinceID
schema.description: Unique identifier for the state or province record (source business key).

schema.name: TerritoryID
schema.description: Identifier of the sales territory the state/province belongs to.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Row-unique GUID assigned by the source system.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Timestamp when the source record was last modified.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 132 requirement(s) and 18 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (7)

- **hub_business_entity** — business key `BusinessEntityID`. Company-wide party (business entity) register; persons share the same business entity number and therefore the same hub (one hub per business key). Integration point for sales, HR, purchasing and marketing. Email addresses and sign-in credentials attach via the same business entity number and are declared as feeds so their satellites bind to their own source relations. Integrated from 4 source(s): BusinessEntity.BusinessEntityID, Person.BusinessEntityID, EmailAddress.BusinessEntityID, Password.BusinessEntityID; canonical staging key column `BUSINESSENTITYID`. _(requirements: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-037, REQ-055, REQ-076)_
- **hub_address** — business key `AddressID`. Postal address identified by its own address number, shareable by several parties. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-007-2)_
- **hub_address_type** — business key `Name`. Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping), keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-067)_
- **hub_contact_type** — business key `Name`. Reference list of contact types (role a person plays for an organisation), keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-037-2, REQ-038-2, REQ-067)_
- **hub_phone_number_type** — business key `PhoneNumberTypeID`. Reference list of phone number types (home, work, mobile). _(requirements: REQ-045, REQ-049, REQ-067)_
- **hub_country_region** — business key `CountryRegionCode`. Country or region identified by its ISO code. _(requirements: REQ-022-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-067)_
- **hub_state_province** — business key `Name`. State or province reference list, keyed on name per decided key. _(requirements: REQ-023-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-067)_

### Links (5)

- **link_business_entity_address** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_address, hub_address_type. Party-address relationship: which address a party uses and in what capacity (address type). Many-to-many. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + AddressID + AddressTypeID (BusinessEntityAddress). _(requirements: REQ-009-2, REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-018-2, REQ-021-2, REQ-055-2)_
- **link_business_entity_contact** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_business_entity (person), hub_contact_type. Contact relationship: organisation (business entity), the person acting as its contact (role-qualified), and the contact type. Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + PersonID + ContactTypeID (BusinessEntityContact). _(requirements: REQ-035-2, REQ-036-2, REQ-037-2, REQ-039-2, REQ-040-2, REQ-041-2, REQ-042-2, REQ-043-2, REQ-046-2, REQ-056-2)_
- **link_business_entity_phone_number_type** — connects hub_business_entity, hub_phone_number_type. A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type (PersonPhone). Unit of work: BusinessEntityID + PhoneNumberTypeID (PersonPhone). _(requirements: REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-062)_
- **link_address_state_province** — connects hub_address, hub_state_province. The state or province an address sits in (country derived via the state). _(requirements: REQ-002-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-029-2)_
- **link_state_province_country_region** — connects hub_state_province, hub_country_region. Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region. _(requirements: REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-005-2)_

### Satellites (17)

- **sat_business_entity_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: ModifiedDate. Business entity existence and last-changed timestamp; rowguid excluded as technical metadata. Source table: BusinessEntity. _(requirements: REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-010)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_name** — on hub_business_entity; payload: PersonType, NameStyle, Title, FirstName, MiddleName, LastName, Suffix, ModifiedDate. Person type and name details with full history. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Ordinary name/contact data, separated from compliance-sensitive consent and sensitive demographics.. _(requirements: REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-034, REQ-051-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_consent** — on hub_business_entity; payload: EmailPromotion. Email promotion preference (marketing consent) with history built by the warehouse. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Compliance-sensitive classification; history tracked separately.. _(requirements: REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-027, REQ-028, REQ-029, REQ-052-2, REQ-073, REQ-074)_
- **sat_business_entity_person_sensitive** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AdditionalContactInfo, Demographics. Additional contact information and demographics (XML), access restricted. Source table: Person. Split rationale: Sensitive data classification and XML data type; restricted separately from name reporting.. _(requirements: REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-069, REQ-070)_
- **sat_business_entity_email** — on hub_business_entity; payload: EmailAddress, ModifiedDate. A person's email addresses, numbered within the person, with history of superseded values. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: EmailAddressID. Source table: EmailAddress. Split rationale: Own source relation at finer grain (several per person); EmailAddress is declared as a feed of the hub.. _(requirements: REQ-035, REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-053-2, REQ-061)_
- **sat_business_entity_credential** — on hub_business_entity; payload: ModifiedDate. Existence and last-change of a person's sign-in credential; hash and salt deliberately excluded. Source table: Password. Split rationale: Separate source (declared as a hub feed); credential values excluded from analytical use.. _(requirements: REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-053, REQ-055, REQ-056, REQ-072)_
- **sat_business_entity_phone_number_type_numbers** — on link_business_entity_phone_number_type; payload: ModifiedDate. Telephone numbers of a person per phone number type, with history. Multi-active satellite, child dependent key: PhoneNumber. Source table: PersonPhone. _(requirements: REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-048, REQ-053-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_address_details** — on link_business_entity_address; payload: ModifiedDate. Last-changed timestamp of the party-address relationship; history of relationships retained. Source table: BusinessEntityAddress. _(requirements: REQ-019-2, REQ-020-2, REQ-055-2)_
- **sat_business_entity_contact_details** — on link_business_entity_contact; payload: ModifiedDate. Last-changed timestamp of the contact relationship; history retained. Source table: BusinessEntityContact. _(requirements: REQ-044-2, REQ-045-2, REQ-056-2)_
- **sat_address_details** — on hub_address; payload: AddressLine1, AddressLine2, City, PostalCode, ModifiedDate. Street, city and postal details of an address with full history. Source table: Address. _(requirements: REQ-002-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-054-2)_
- **sat_address_location** — on hub_address; payload: SpatialLocation. Geographic location (latitude/longitude) of an address. Source table: Address. Split rationale: Spatial data type and personal-data classification (geographic coordinates).. _(requirements: REQ-004-2, REQ-065, REQ-069)_
- **sat_address_type_details** — on hub_address_type; payload: ModifiedDate. Address type reference metadata. Source table: AddressType. _(requirements: REQ-016-2)_
- **sat_contact_type_details** — on hub_contact_type; payload: ModifiedDate. Contact type reference metadata. Source table: ContactType. _(requirements: REQ-038-2)_
- **sat_phone_number_type_details** — on hub_phone_number_type; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Phone number type name, with history of renames. Source table: PhoneNumberType. _(requirements: REQ-045, REQ-049)_
- **sat_country_region_details** — on hub_country_region; payload: Name, ModifiedDate. Country or region name with visible rename history. Source table: CountryRegion. _(requirements: REQ-022-2, REQ-032-2, REQ-033-2, REQ-034-2)_
- **sat_state_province_details** — on hub_state_province; payload: StateProvinceCode, IsOnlyStateProvinceFlag, ModifiedDate. State or province ISO code and no-genuine-code flag. Source table: StateProvince. _(requirements: REQ-023-2, REQ-026-2, REQ-027-2, REQ-032-2, REQ-066)_
- **sat_state_province_territory** — on hub_state_province; payload: TerritoryID. Sales territory assignment of a state or province, history preserved; territory descriptions come from the sales area. Source table: StateProvince. Split rationale: Different rate of change and business meaning (territory reassignment) from code/flag details.. _(requirements: REQ-028-2, REQ-029-2, REQ-030-2, REQ-031-2, REQ-057)_
